title: Scalable Personal Signal hover metadata in the native YEIS galaxy

scope.subject: Desktop hover discovery for Personal Signal points without a second picking or tooltip framework

research_summary: Reuse existing Three.js projection and the hosted R3F Canvas surface to identify nearby Personal Signal points in screen space. Keep the label as a simple non-interactive React overlay; do not add Floating UI or retrofit R3F raycast handlers onto imperative YEIS Points solely for hover.

sources.finding: React Three Fiber provides a mature raycast-backed pointer-event system for scene objects that register pointer handlers, but the hosted YEIS sky points are imperative renderer objects rather than JSX interaction nodes.
Three.js provides Vector3 camera projection, which can convert the already-known Personal Signal sky directions into normalized screen coordinates using the active camera.

Floating UI supports virtual point/cursor anchors for collision-aware floating DOM positioning, but it does not solve WebGL signal identification and would add a dependency for a simple non-interactive label.

search_ladder.conclusion: A full onboarding or annotation product would exceed this narrow hover-label implementation and still require the same WebGL signal hit detection.
The existing React Three Fiber host already supplies a Canvas and pointer/raycast framework, so no second rendering or input framework should be introduced.
This hover path is a small interaction implementation inside the existing YEIS galaxy renderer rather than a standalone reusable subsystem.
Three.js camera projection directly solves 3D-to-screen mapping; Floating UI virtual elements are a mature alternative for DOM positioning but are unnecessary for this bounded non-interactive card.

candidates.name: React Three Fiber raycast pointer events
candidates.reason: Useful for declarative R3F objects, but the Personal Signal sky is owned by imperative YEIS Points. Retrofitting event-handler registration or duplicate hit meshes solely for hover would add scene objects and interaction ownership.

candidates.name: Three.js Vector3.project plus existing Canvas pointer coordinates
candidates.reason: Uses the active YEIS/R3F camera and known Personal Signal positions directly, adds no dependency or duplicate 3D geometry, and can share the same point list used for rendering/picking.

candidates.name: Floating UI virtual-point tooltip
candidates.reason: Excellent after a DOM/reference point is already known, but it does not identify the hovered WebGL signal. For a small non-interactive card, adding its positioning runtime duplicates simple viewport clamping.

decision.rationale: Use the Three.js projection primitive already loaded by the universe renderer and the existing Canvas pointer surface. This solves the actual WebGL-to-screen mapping with no new dependency, preserves YEIS as spatial authority, and leaves touch/coarse-pointer interaction on the existing direct-picking path.

higher_level_tradeoffs.reason: R3F is the broader host framework but its declarative raycast event path would require adapting imperative YEIS points into separate interactive objects; direct projection is narrower and reuses the same authoritative signal positions without a parallel hit scene.

decision.fallback: If hover cards become interactive, require collision-aware placement, or multiple overlay surfaces compete, re-evaluate Floating UI virtual elements before extending custom positioning logic.
